goals: Mechanistic: quantify elevation-resolved partitioning of water into ET, surface runoff, and sub-surface drainage/recharge, including snow storage/melt, across the Bow headwaters
Validation: compare simulated streamflow/snow against in-domain observations

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves the water-balance terms requested; a spatial sample across the catchment is the intended way to span heterogeneity. However the primary driver (elevation) is not representable without downscaled forcing, and no forcing covers this Canadian domain.

answerable: Soil-texture control on partitioning under a SINGLE representative forcing (fallback only — does NOT isolate the elevation/climate signal the user asked for), CONTINGENT on a Canada-capable forcing product being ingested first

not_answerable.why: Elevation acts through T/P lapse rates and the rain-snow transition; the stack cannot downscale forcing by elevation, so an elevation-stratified column set under uniform forcing would vary by soil, not elevation. Signal cannot be isolated.

not_answerable.aspect: Running ANY ELM column in the Bow headwaters
not_answerable.why: NLDAS is CONUS-only; the domain is in Alberta, Canada. No forcing product in the stack covers this domain.
not_answerable.needs: Canada-capable atmospheric forcing dataset (e.g. ERA5-Land / RDRS / WFDE5) ingest

not_answerable.why: Snow/SWE is central to this relief but is neither downscaled nor validated in-domain.
not_answerable.needs: snow/SWE output validation dataset for Canada

not_answerable.why: ECCC gauges are not ingestible in the stack, and point-column output would need routing/aggregation to a gauge.

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (fallback design only — records the soil axis the stack CAN pull once forcing exists; elevation bands listed but NOT resolvable under uniform forcing)
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands x 3 dominant soils = 9 columns would span the catchment's stratification IF forcing were downscaled; presented as the target design, but it does NOT resolve elevation under the current uniform-forcing limit. N kept small and defensible rather than a blind grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate at the rain-snow transition (subalpine band) where melt timing dominates partitioning, and in valley bottoms where soil-moisture/recharge exchange is strongest. Downstream expander samples real DEM/soil rasters within each band.
sampling_strategy.replication: None until the forcing/downscaling blockers are resolved; replication is not justified while the primary driver is unrepresentable.

sampling_plan.reason: Low-elevation baseline; rain-dominated, deepest recharge pathways — anchors the low end of the (aspirational) elevation gradient.

Rain-snow transition — the elevation band where melt timing most controls partitioning; highest-priority group.
Isolates soil effect within the critical rain-snow transition band.
Shallow-soil melt response at the transition; captures fast runoff vs storage tradeoff.
Snow-dominated headwater generation zone; upper end of the gradient.
Alpine coarse-substrate recharge behaviour under snowmelt.
Completes low-band soil coverage for the soil-only fallback comparison.
Completes high-band soil coverage; rare but present in cirque basins.

none — SNOTEL is US-only, no coverage in Alberta

assumptions: Dominant soil classes (coarse glacial-till, fine valley-fill, thin alpine regolith) are placeholders; actual classes come from a gridded soil raster the expander samples.
Elevation bands (montane/subalpine/alpine) are physically motivated but cannot be dynamically distinguished under uniform forcing.
No in-stack forcing or observations currently cover this Canadian domain; the design is presented as a target contingent on the backlog above.
